modules.src:
###
post: Dormand and Prince's explicit 5(4) pair
agent: claude

Seven stages give a fifth-order solution and an embedded fourth-order one;
their difference estimates the local error, and the step is accepted when
that error, weighted by atol + rtol |y|, has RMS norm below 1. The seventh
stage is evaluated at the new point, so it is the next step's first stage
("first same as last"): six evaluations per step.

The step controller is the elementary one SciPy's RK45 uses: the next step
is h (0.9 / err)^(1/5), changed by at most a factor 10 up and 5 down, and
not grown right after a rejection. The dense output is Hairer's
fifth-order continuous extension, from the stages already computed.

Each accepted step also estimates h |lambda|, the step times the stiffest
eigenvalue the stages saw (Hairer's test, Solving ODEs II, IV.2): 15 steps
in a row with h |lambda| above 3.25 mark the problem stiff, which `method =
AUTO` uses to change to Radau IIA.

J. R. Dormand and P. J. Prince, A family of embedded Runge-Kutta formulae,
Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 6, 19-26 (1980), doi:10.1016/0771-050X(80)90013-3.
###

from ode.core import (
    Dense, OdeCfg, OdeState, DOPRI5, MAX_FACTOR, MIN_FACTOR, NOT_FINITE, SAFETY, STEP_TOO_SMALL,
    all_finite, min_step_at,
)

# the nodes
C2 = 1.0 / 5.0
C3 = 3.0 / 10.0
C4 = 4.0 / 5.0
C5 = 8.0 / 9.0
# the stage weights a_ij
A21 = 1.0 / 5.0
A31 = 3.0 / 40.0
A32 = 9.0 / 40.0
A41 = 44.0 / 45.0
A42 = -56.0 / 15.0
A43 = 32.0 / 9.0
A51 = 19372.0 / 6561.0
A52 = -25360.0 / 2187.0
A53 = 64448.0 / 6561.0
A54 = -212.0 / 729.0
A61 = 9017.0 / 3168.0
A62 = -355.0 / 33.0
A63 = 46732.0 / 5247.0
A64 = 49.0 / 176.0
A65 = -5103.0 / 18656.0
# the fifth-order weights (also row 7 of the tableau)
B1 = 35.0 / 384.0
B3 = 500.0 / 1113.0
B4 = 125.0 / 192.0
B5 = -2187.0 / 6784.0
B6 = 11.0 / 84.0
# fifth-order minus fourth-order weights: the error estimate
E1 = -71.0 / 57600.0
E3 = 71.0 / 16695.0
E4 = -71.0 / 1920.0
E5 = 17253.0 / 339200.0
E6 = -22.0 / 525.0
E7 = 1.0 / 40.0
# the dense output's fifth-order correction (Hairer's d_i)
D1 = -12715105075.0 / 11282082432.0
D3 = 87487479700.0 / 32700410799.0
D4 = -10690763975.0 / 1880347072.0
D5 = 701980252875.0 / 199316789632.0
D6 = -1453857185.0 / 822651844.0
D7 = 69997945.0 / 29380423.0
# the controller's exponent, -1 / (order of the error estimate + 1)
ERR_EXPONENT = -1.0 / 5.0
# rhs evaluations per step (the seventh is reused)
STAGE_EVALS: Int = 6
# the dense output's coefficient rows
DENSE_ROWS = 5
# the stiffness test: h |lambda| above this bound, this many steps in a row
STIFF_BOUND = 3.25
STIFF_STEPS: Int = 15
# this many non-stiff steps in a row forget a stiff run
NONSTIFF_RESET: Int = 6

#| One accepted Dormand-Prince step from s, retrying with smaller steps
#| until the error test passes. Returns the state at the new point, with its
#| dense output; status STEP_TOO_SMALL when the step underflows.
def dopri_step(f, s0: OdeState, c: OdeCfg, p: Arr) -> OdeState {
    s = s0
    t = s.t
    y = s.y
    k1 = s.fy
    n = len(y)
    min_step = min_step_at(t)
    h_abs = min(s.h_abs, c.max_step)
    if h_abs < min_step {
        h_abs = min_step
    }
    rejected = false
    accepted = false
    h_next = h_abs
    while not accepted {
        if h_abs < min_step {
            s.status = STEP_TOO_SMALL
            return s
        }
        t_new = t + h_abs * s.dir
        if s.dir * (t_new - c.t_bound) > 0.0 {
            t_new = c.t_bound
        }
        h = t_new - t
        h_abs = abs(h)
        #: the six new stages (element loops: no temporary arrays in the hot path)
        yt = zeros(n)
        for i to n {
            yt[i] = y[i] + h * (A21 * k1[i])
        }
        k2 = f(t + C2 * h, yt, p)
        for i to n {
            yt[i] = y[i] + h * (A31 * k1[i] + A32 * k2[i])
        }
        k3 = f(t + C3 * h, yt, p)
        for i to n {
            yt[i] = y[i] + h * (A41 * k1[i] + A42 * k2[i] + A43 * k3[i])
        }
        k4 = f(t + C4 * h, yt, p)
        for i to n {
            yt[i] = y[i] + h * (A51 * k1[i] + A52 * k2[i] + A53 * k3[i] + A54 * k4[i])
        }
        k5 = f(t + C5 * h, yt, p)
        y6 = zeros(n)
        for i to n {
            y6[i] = y[i] + h * (A61 * k1[i] + A62 * k2[i] + A63 * k3[i] + A64 * k4[i] + A65 * k5[i])
        }
        k6 = f(t + h, y6, p)
        y_new = zeros(n)
        for i to n {
            y_new[i] = y[i] + h * (B1 * k1[i] + B3 * k3[i] + B4 * k4[i] + B5 * k5[i] + B6 * k6[i])
        }
        k7 = f(t + h, y_new, p)
        s.nfev += STAGE_EVALS
        if not all_finite(y_new) {
            s.status = NOT_FINITE
            return s
        }
        #: the error test, in the weighted RMS norm
        acc = 0.0
        for i to n {
            e = h * (E1 * k1[i] + E3 * k3[i] + E4 * k4[i] + E5 * k5[i] + E6 * k6[i] + E7 * k7[i])
            w = e / (c.atol[i] + max(abs(y[i]), abs(y_new[i])) * c.rtol)
            acc += w * w
        }
        err_norm = sqrt(acc / n)
        if err_norm < 1.0 {
            factor = MAX_FACTOR
            if err_norm > 0.0 {
                factor = min(MAX_FACTOR, SAFETY * pow(err_norm, ERR_EXPONENT))
            }
            if rejected {
                factor = min(1.0, factor)
            }
            h_next = h_abs * factor
            accepted = true
            #: Hairer's stiffness estimate: h |lambda| ~ h |k7 - k6| / |y_new - y6|
            num2 = 0.0
            den2 = 0.0
            for i to n {
                num2 += (k7[i] - k6[i]) * (k7[i] - k6[i])
                den2 += (y_new[i] - y6[i]) * (y_new[i] - y6[i])
            }
            if den2 > 0.0 {
                hlamb = abs(h) * sqrt(num2 / den2)
                if hlamb > STIFF_BOUND {
                    s.nonstiff_count = 0
                    s.stiff_count += 1
                    if s.stiff_count >= STIFF_STEPS {
                        s.stiff = true
                    }
                }
                else {
                    s.nonstiff_count += 1
                    if s.nonstiff_count >= NONSTIFF_RESET {
                        s.stiff_count = 0
                    }
                }
            }
            #: the dense output's coefficients
            Q = zeros(DENSE_ROWS, n)
            for i to n {
                ydiff = y_new[i] - y[i]
                bspl = h * k1[i] - ydiff
                Q[0, i] = y[i]
                Q[1, i] = ydiff
                Q[2, i] = bspl
                Q[3, i] = ydiff - h * k7[i] - bspl
                Q[4, i] = h * (D1 * k1[i] + D3 * k3[i] + D4 * k4[i] + D5 * k5[i] + D6 * k6[i] + D7 * k7[i])
            }
            s.dense = Dense { kind: DOPRI5, t_old: t, t_new: t_new, h: h, Q: Q, y_old: y, order: 0 }
            s.has_dense = true
            s.t = t_new
            s.y = y_new
            s.fy = k7
        }
        else {
            h_abs = h_abs * max(MIN_FACTOR, SAFETY * pow(err_norm, ERR_EXPONENT))
            rejected = true
            s.nreject += 1
        }
    }
    s.h_abs = h_next
    s.naccept += 1
    return s
}

test "the tableau is consistent: rows sum to the nodes, the weights to 1" {
    assert_near(A21, C2, 1.0e-16)
    assert_near(A31 + A32, C3, 1.0e-16)
    assert_near(A41 + A42 + A43, C4, 1.0e-15)
    assert_near(A51 + A52 + A53 + A54, C5, 1.0e-14)
    assert_near(A61 + A62 + A63 + A64 + A65, 1.0, 1.0e-14)
    assert_near(B1 + B3 + B4 + B5 + B6, 1.0, 1.0e-15)
    # the embedded fourth-order weights also sum to 1, so the error weights sum to 0
    assert_near(E1 + E3 + E4 + E5 + E6 + E7, 0.0, 1.0e-16)
    # the fifth-order weights integrate t^4 exactly: sum b_i c_i^4 = 1/5
    assert_near(B3 * pow(C3, 4.0) + B4 * pow(C4, 4.0) + B5 * pow(C5, 4.0) + B6, 0.2, 1.0e-15)
}

modules.src:
###
post: Radau IIA of order 5, after Hairer and Wanner's RADAU5
agent: claude

The three-stage Radau IIA method is collocation at the right Radau points
c = ((4 - sqrt 6)/10, (4 + sqrt 6)/10, 1): the step solves for the stage
increments Z_i = y(t + c_i h) - y(t) from

    Z = h (A (x) I) F(Z),        F_i = f(t + c_i h, y + Z_i)

by simplified Newton iterations, all with the Jacobian J at the start of the
step. The trick that makes it affordable is to diagonalize A^-1 = T Lambda
T^-1: in W = (T^-1 (x) I) Z the 3n-by-3n Newton matrix splits into one real
system (mu_1/h - J) and one complex system ((alpha + i beta)/h - J), so a
step costs one real and one complex LU (here the complex one is written as
its real 2n-by-2n form). The new point is y + Z_3; the method is order 5,
L-stable, and stiffly accurate.

The error estimate is the embedded formula of Hairer and Wanner (Solving
ODEs II, IV.8, eq. 8.20): (mu_1/h - J)^-1 (f(t, y) + sum_i e_i Z_i / h),
filtered once more through the real system after a rejection. The step
size follows Gustafsson's predictive controller; the Newton iteration stops
on Hairer's convergence-rate test, and a failed iteration halves the step
after first refreshing a stale Jacobian. The constants are SciPy's
(scipy/integrate/_ivp/radau.py), which carries Hairer's RADAU5 logic.

E. Hairer and G. Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations II: Stiff
and Differential-Algebraic Problems, 2nd ed., Springer (1996),
doi:10.1007/978-3-642-05221-7.
###

from ode.core import (
    Dense, OdeCfg, OdeState, MAX_FACTOR, MIN_FACTOR, NOT_FINITE, RADAU, STEP_TOO_SMALL,
    all_finite, jacobian, dense_at, min_step_at, rms,
)
from ode.lu import lu_factor, lu_solve

S6 = sqrt(6.0)
# the collocation nodes
C1 = (4.0 - S6) / 10.0
C2 = (4.0 + S6) / 10.0
C3 = 1.0
# the error estimate's weights on Z
ER1 = (-13.0 - 7.0 * S6) / 3.0
ER2 = (-13.0 + 7.0 * S6) / 3.0
ER3 = -1.0 / 3.0
# the eigenvalues of A^-1: one real, one complex pair alpha -+ i beta
MU_REAL = 3.0 + pow(3.0, 2.0 / 3.0) - pow(3.0, 1.0 / 3.0)
MU_RE = 3.0 + 0.5 * (pow(3.0, 1.0 / 3.0) - pow(3.0, 2.0 / 3.0))
MU_IM = -0.5 * (pow(3.0, 5.0 / 6.0) + pow(3.0, 7.0 / 6.0))
# T and T^-1, which diagonalize A^-1 (block-diagonally for the complex pair)
T = [[0.09443876248897524, -0.14125529502095421, 0.03002919410514742],
     [0.25021312296533332, 0.20412935229379994, -0.38294211275726192],
     [1.0, 1.0, 0.0]]
TI = [[4.17871859155190428, 0.32768282076106237, 0.52337644549944951],
      [-4.17871859155190428, -0.32768282076106237, 0.47662355450055044],
      [0.50287263494578682, -2.57192694985560522, 0.59603920482822492]]
# the collocation polynomial: y(t + x h) = y + sum_j (sum_i P[i, j] Z_i) x^(j+1)
P = [[13.0 / 3.0 + 7.0 * S6 / 3.0, -23.0 / 3.0 - 22.0 * S6 / 3.0, 10.0 / 3.0 + 5.0 * S6],
     [13.0 / 3.0 - 7.0 * S6 / 3.0, -23.0 / 3.0 + 22.0 * S6 / 3.0, 10.0 / 3.0 - 5.0 * S6],
     [1.0 / 3.0, -8.0 / 3.0, 10.0 / 3.0]]
NSTAGES: Int = 3
NEWTON_MAXITER: Int = 6
# a Jacobian is refreshed after a step whose Newton iteration converged slower than this
JAC_RATE = 1.0e-3
# a step is not changed by less than this factor (keeps the LU factors)
KEEP_STEP = 1.2

#| Factor the real system mu_1/h - J into LU1 and the complex system
#| (alpha + i beta)/h - J, as the real block matrix [[aI - J, -bI], [bI, aI - J]],
#| into LU2.
def radau_factor(s0: OdeState, h: Num) -> OdeState {
    s = s0
    n = len(s.y)
    s.LU1 = MU_REAL / h * eye(n) - s.J
    ok1 = lu_factor(s.LU1, s.piv1)
    a = MU_RE / h
    b = MU_IM / h
    M = zeros(2 * n, 2 * n)
    for i to n {
        for j to n {
            M[i, j] = -s.J[i, j]
            M[n + i, n + j] = -s.J[i, j]
        }
        M[i, i] += a
        M[n + i, n + i] += a
        M[i, n + i] = -b
        M[n + i, i] = b
    }
    ok2 = lu_factor(M, s.piv2)
    s.LU2 = M
    s.have_lu = true
    s.nlu += 2
    return s
}

#| Simplified Newton on the collocation equations, in the transformed
#| variables W = T^-1 Z. Returns whether it converged, the iterations, Z
#| (3 by n), the last contraction rate (-1 when there was none) and the rhs
#| evaluations it made.
def radau_newton(f, s: OdeState, h: Num, Z0: Arr, scale: Arr, tol: Num, p: Arr) {
    n = len(s.y)
    a = MU_RE / h
    b = MU_IM / h
    mr = MU_REAL / h
    Z = copy(Z0)
    W = TI @ Z0
    F = zeros(NSTAGES, n)
    cs = [C1, C2, C3]
    norm_old = -1.0
    rate = -1.0
    converged = false
    iters: Int = 0
    nfev: Int = 0
    going = true
    yt = zeros(n)
    f_real = zeros(n)
    rc = zeros(2 * n)
    while going and iters < NEWTON_MAXITER {
        finite = true
        for i to NSTAGES {
            for j to n {
                yt[j] = s.y[j] + Z[i, j]
            }
            fi = f(s.t + cs[i] * h, yt, p)
            for j to n {
                F[i, j] = fi[j]
            }
            finite = finite and all_finite(fi)
        }
        nfev += NSTAGES
        iters += 1
        if not finite {
            going = false
        }
        else {
            #: the right sides of the real and the complex system, from G = T^-1 F
            for j to n {
                g0 = TI[0, 0] * F[0, j] + TI[0, 1] * F[1, j] + TI[0, 2] * F[2, j]
                g1 = TI[1, 0] * F[0, j] + TI[1, 1] * F[1, j] + TI[1, 2] * F[2, j]
                g2 = TI[2, 0] * F[0, j] + TI[2, 1] * F[1, j] + TI[2, 2] * F[2, j]
                f_real[j] = g0 - mr * W[0, j]
                rc[j] = g1 - (a * W[1, j] - b * W[2, j])
                rc[n + j] = g2 - (a * W[2, j] + b * W[1, j])
            }
            dW0 = lu_solve(s.LU1, s.piv1, f_real)
            dc = lu_solve(s.LU2, s.piv2, rc)
            acc = 0.0
            for j to n {
                u0 = dW0[j] / scale[j]
                u1 = dc[j] / scale[j]
                u2 = dc[n + j] / scale[j]
                acc += u0 * u0 + u1 * u1 + u2 * u2
            }
            dnorm = sqrt(acc / (NSTAGES * n))
            if norm_old >= 0.0 {
                rate = dnorm / norm_old
            }
            #: stop early when the contraction cannot reach tol in the iterations left
            if rate >= 0.0 and (rate >= 1.0 or pow(rate, NEWTON_MAXITER - iters + 1) / (1.0 - rate) * dnorm > tol) {
                going = false
            }
            else {
                for j to n {
                    W[0, j] += dW0[j]
                    W[1, j] += dc[j]
                    W[2, j] += dc[n + j]
                    for i to NSTAGES {
                        Z[i, j] = T[i, 0] * W[0, j] + T[i, 1] * W[1, j] + T[i, 2] * W[2, j]
                    }
                }
                if dnorm == 0.0 or (rate >= 0.0 and rate / (1.0 - rate) * dnorm < tol) {
                    converged = true
                    going = false
                }
                norm_old = dnorm
            }
        }
    }
    return converged, iters, Z, rate, nfev
}

#| Gustafsson's predictive step factor (Hairer and Wanner II, IV.8, eq. 8.25),
#| err^(-1/4) scaled by how the last two steps' errors moved.
def predict_factor(h_abs: Num, h_abs_old: Num, err: Num, err_old: Num) -> Num {
    mult = 1.0
    if err_old > 0.0 and h_abs_old > 0.0 and err > 0.0 {
        mult = h_abs / h_abs_old * pow(err_old / err, 0.25)
    }
    if err == 0.0 {
        return MAX_FACTOR
    }
    return min(1.0, mult) * pow(err, -0.25)
}

#| One accepted Radau IIA step from s, with the given Jacobian source.
def radau_step(f, jac, s0: OdeState, c: OdeCfg, p: Arr) -> OdeState {
    s = s0
    t = s.t
    y = s.y
    n = len(y)
    min_step = min_step_at(t)
    h_abs = s.h_abs
    if h_abs > c.max_step {
        h_abs = c.max_step
        s.h_abs_old = 0.0
        s.err_old = -1.0
        s.have_lu = false
    }
    else {
        if h_abs < min_step {
            h_abs = min_step
            s.h_abs_old = 0.0
            s.err_old = -1.0
            s.have_lu = false
        }
    }
    cs = [C1, C2, C3]
    ew = [ER1, ER2, ER3]
    rejected = false
    accepted = false
    h = 0.0
    t_new = t
    Z = zeros(NSTAGES, n)
    iters: Int = 0
    rate = -1.0
    err_norm = 0.0
    safety = 0.0
    y_new = y
    while not accepted {
        if h_abs < min_step {
            s.status = STEP_TOO_SMALL
            return s
        }
        t_new = t + h_abs * s.dir
        if s.dir * (t_new - c.t_bound) > 0.0 {
            t_new = c.t_bound
        }
        h = t_new - t
        h_abs = abs(h)
        #: the starting guess: the last step's collocation polynomial, extrapolated
        Z0 = zeros(NSTAGES, n)
        if s.has_dense and s.dense.kind == RADAU {
            for i to NSTAGES {
                Z0[i, :] = dense_at(s.dense, t + h * cs[i]) - y
            }
        }
        scale = c.atol + abs(y) * c.rtol
        converged = false
        trying = true
        while trying {
            if not s.have_lu {
                s = radau_factor(s, h)
            }
            converged, iters, Z, rate, nf = radau_newton(f, s, h, Z0, scale, c.newton_tol, p)
            s.nfev += nf
            if converged or s.jac_current {
                trying = false
            }
            else {
                #: a stale Jacobian may be why: refresh it and try again
                Jn, nj = jacobian(f, jac, t, y, s.fy, p, c)
                s.J = Jn
                s.nfev += nj
                s.njev += 1
                s.jac_current = true
                s.have_lu = false
            }
        }
        if not converged {
            h_abs = 0.5 * h_abs
            s.have_lu = false
            s.nreject += 1
            rejected = true
        }
        else {
            y_new = y + Z[NSTAGES - 1, :]
            ZE = zeros(n)
            for i to NSTAGES {
                ZE = ZE + ew[i] * Z[i, :]
            }
            ZE = ZE / h
            err = lu_solve(s.LU1, s.piv1, s.fy + ZE)
            scale = c.atol + max(abs(y), abs(y_new)) * c.rtol
            err_norm = rms(err / scale)
            safety = 0.9 * (2.0 * NEWTON_MAXITER + 1.0) / (2.0 * NEWTON_MAXITER + iters)
            if rejected and err_norm > 1.0 {
                err = lu_solve(s.LU1, s.piv1, f(t, y + err, p) + ZE)
                s.nfev += 1
                err_norm = rms(err / scale)
            }
            if err_norm > 1.0 {
                factor = predict_factor(h_abs, s.h_abs_old, err_norm, s.err_old)
                h_abs = h_abs * max(MIN_FACTOR, safety * factor)
                s.have_lu = false
                s.nreject += 1
                rejected = true
            }
            else {
                accepted = true
            }
        }
    }
    if not all_finite(y_new) {
        s.status = NOT_FINITE
        return s
    }
    #: the next step: refresh J when Newton was slow, keep the LU when h barely changes
    recompute_jac = iters > 2 and rate > JAC_RATE
    factor = predict_factor(h_abs, s.h_abs_old, err_norm, s.err_old)
    factor = min(MAX_FACTOR, safety * factor)
    if not recompute_jac and factor < KEEP_STEP {
        factor = 1.0
    }
    else {
        s.have_lu = false
    }
    f_new = f(t_new, y_new, p)
    s.nfev += 1
    if recompute_jac {
        Jn, nj = jacobian(f, jac, t_new, y_new, f_new, p, c)
        s.J = Jn
        s.nfev += nj
        s.njev += 1
        s.jac_current = true
    }
    else {
        s.jac_current = false
    }
    #: the dense output: the collocation polynomial's coefficients P^T Z
    Q = transpose(P) @ Z
    s.dense = Dense { kind: RADAU, t_old: t, t_new: t_new, h: h, Q: Q, y_old: y, order: NSTAGES }
    s.has_dense = true
    s.h_abs_old = h_abs
    s.err_old = err_norm
    s.h_abs = h_abs * factor
    s.t = t_new
    s.y = y_new
    s.fy = f_new
    s.naccept += 1
    return s
}

test "T and its inverse, and the collocation polynomial through the stages" {
    assert_allclose(TI @ T, eye(NSTAGES), 1.0e-15)
    # sum_j P[i, j] c_k^(j+1) = delta_ik: the polynomial hits Z_k at c_k
    cs = [C1, C2, C3]
    V = zeros(NSTAGES, NSTAGES)
    V[:, 0] = cs
    V[:, 1] = cs * cs
    V[:, 2] = cs * cs * cs
    assert_allclose(P @ transpose(V), eye(NSTAGES), 1.0e-13)
    # the real eigenvalue of A^-1 and the complex pair's modulus: det A^-1 = 60
    assert_near(MU_REAL * (MU_RE * MU_RE + MU_IM * MU_IM), 60.0, 1.0e-12)
}
